world.h: France suspends high school classes for week
world.b: France's prime minister suspended high school classes nationwide for the rest of the week as protesters clashed with police.
more: Authorities counted about 250,000 protesters Tuesday; organizers said closer to half a million.
Students are protesting crowded classrooms, teacher shortages and run-down buildings.

world.h: Drones hit two ships off Bulgaria, one sinks
world.b: Sea and aerial drones hit two commercial ships in the Black Sea off Bulgaria, sinking one and wounding several people.
more: Prime Minister Rumen Radev called the attack 'absolutely unacceptable.'
Bulgaria is searching for missing crew about 70 nautical miles off its coast.

world.b: The Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed 4,000 in what Democracy Now! calls the fastest-growing outbreak on record.
more: Health officials believe it began in January but was not detected until May.
Democracy Now! reports that Trump's USAID cuts have fueled the outbreak.

world.b: The Parti Quebecois won the most seats in Quebec's election and will form the province's next government.
more: Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, set to become premier, promised a third referendum on leaving Canada in his first term.
It was not yet clear whether the party reached the 64 seats needed for a majority.

world.b: A worker at a Siberian anti-plague institute died of what Russia calls pneumonia of unknown cause, fueling plague concerns.
more: A local official earlier said she died 'possibly from plague.'
Secretary of State Rubio said it's not cause for alarm but is 'cause for focus,' and Trump offered US help.

world.h: Ship sinks in Romanian waters; Kyiv blames Russian drone
world.b: Romania said two people died and 11 were rescued when a grain ship caught fire and sank in its Black Sea waters.
more: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy blamed a Russian drone attack.

world.h: Brazil's presidential race heads to a runoff
world.b: Flávio Bolsonaro took 47% and President Lula 45% in Sunday's first round, so the two meet in a runoff on October 25.
more: Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest after a conviction for plotting a coup.

world.h: Iran says Strait of Hormuz stays closed
world.b: Tehran said the waterway will stay closed until the US meets conditions from their June agreement in Islamabad.
more: Iran's demands include ending the war, lifting blockades and sanctions, releasing frozen assets and paying compensation.
Iran also said there is no military solution to its conflict with the US.

world.h: Spain calls snap election amid housing protests
world.b: Tens of thousands marched in Madrid and other cities over housing, and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called elections for November 29.
more: Lawmakers had rejected his housing measures.
Tens of thousands marched; police in Valencia used tear gas and rubber bullets near a real estate summit, after an 87-year-old woman's eviction sparked anger.

national.b: Jim Bakker, who built the 'PTL Club' televangelism empire with Tammy Faye before losing it to scandal, has died at 86.
more: His wife Lori Bakker announced his death; the cause was not immediately clear.
He had hosted 'The Jim Bakker Show' near Branson, Missouri, since 2003.

national.h: Disney, ABC take on Trump's FCC in court
national.b: Disney and the FCC face off in a Washington federal court Tuesday over how far First Amendment protections reach.
more: Trump has repeatedly called for ABC to fire late-night host Jimmy Kimmel and has attacked 'The View.'

national.h: FBI spy-hunting squads hit with deep cuts
national.b: FBI counterintelligence squads have been sharply cut nationwide even as espionage threats grow, five people familiar told NPR.
more: In many of the FBI's 56 field offices, only 50% to 60% of counterintelligence positions are filled.
In several offices the number of these squads has been cut in half.

national.h: Protesters smash Cornell door over rape case
national.b: Protesters broke a glass door and spray-painted Cornell's administration building early Monday amid anger over a 2024 gang rape case.

national.h: Supreme Court hears Boulder climate damages case
national.b: On the first day of its new term, the Supreme Court heard Boulder County's case seeking damages from oil and gas companies for climate-linked disasters.
more: Boulder County is one of dozens of US jurisdictions suing the industry over the cost of climate damage.

national.h: Court turns away 'Let's Go Brandon' shirt appeal
national.b: The Supreme Court rejected a Michigan mother's appeal over a school's ban on her sons' 'Let's Go Brandon' sweatshirts.
more: A lower court had ruled the phrase's veiled vulgarity lets schools ban it.

national.h: Oil company plugs well near Enid's water supply
national.b: An Oklahoma company permanently sealed a wastewater disposal well a quarter-mile from Enid's public water wells, ProPublica reports.
more: The Frontier and ProPublica found regulators approved the well in 2018 without the hearing state rules require.

national.h: Judge halts border wall work in Big Bend
national.b: Federal Judge Kathleen Cardone blocked further border wall construction inside Big Bend National Park.
more: She signaled that constitutional claims against the wall are likely to succeed.

national.h: Tennessee prison chief resigns after execution
national.b: Frank Strada is stepping down after the botched execution attempt of Christa Pike, who remains in critical condition.
more: Democracy Now! reports it was his fifth failed execution in two states since 2022.

national.b: Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff welcomed an independent law firm investigation into a 2024 gang rape case.
more: The New York attorney general is also running a criminal investigation.

national.h: Search ends for six aboard crashed medical jet
national.b: The Coast Guard suspended its search for six people aboard a medical jet that crashed on a flight from Bermuda to Boston.
more: The passengers were a Bermudian mother and son; the four crew members were Canadian.

politics.h: Trump draws criticism for 'take out LA' remark
politics.b: At a Nebraska rally, Trump said Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego, calling it 'a very small price to pay.'
more: The crowd laughed and cheered; Gov. Gavin Newsom was among the critics.
The White House said he meant he wants to stop Iran from having that capability.

politics.b: The Justice Department filed 40 new cases seeking to strip citizenship from naturalized Americans, a number it calls a record.
more: Prosecutors say the targets are accused of crimes such as money laundering, child sexual abuse, visa fraud and tax evasion.
The petitions were filed from late August through early October.

politics.b: Justice Samuel Alito said the Supreme Court can do little to slow the surge in emergency appeals under Trump.
more: Emergency applications now rival the number of fully briefed cases the court hears each year.

politics.h: Abrego Garcia back in court over Liberia deportation
politics.b: Kilmar Abrego Garcia returns to federal court as the government tries to lift an order blocking his deportation to Liberia.
more: His case began when he was mistakenly deported to El Salvador last year.
His lawyers want Judge Paula Xinis to make the injunction permanent.

politics.h: Musk, Luckey Pentagon roles raise ethics worries
politics.b: A new Pentagon study of AI-powered weapons led by Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey is raising conflict-of-interest concerns.
more: Hegseth announced 'Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare' last week; Newt Gingrich also leads it.
The study is expected to take 120 days.

politics.h: Tillis calls Hegseth vote his 'biggest regret'
politics.b: In a new book, GOP Sen. Thom Tillis says his deciding vote to confirm Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is the biggest regret of his career.
more: He also writes that he 'should've stopped' Robert F. Kennedy Jr. from becoming health secretary.

politics.h: Trump blames refineries, not Iran war, for gas prices
politics.b: Trump blamed Democrats and Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries for high US fuel prices, not the war with Iran.

politics.h: Obama to rally with El-Sayed in Detroit
politics.b: Former President Obama will campaign with Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed at an October 24 rally in Detroit.
more: Obama also taped two dozen ads for Democratic candidates for governor and Senate.

politics.h: Trump campaigns for Ricketts in Nebraska
politics.b: President Trump is rallying in Grand Island, Nebraska, for Sen. Pete Ricketts, who faces independent Dan Osborn.
more: Trump calls it part of a 32-day blitz of rallies before the November 3 election.

politics.h: Trump names Jay Clayton AI czar
politics.b: President Trump picked Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead a new 'Super Intelligence Force' for federal AI work.
more: An OpenAI safety staffer, David Robinson, recently resigned saying the company 'isn't being nearly careful enough.'

politics.h: KKK tries to rebrand as the 'Knights Party'
politics.b: The hate group is trying to rebrand itself as the Knights Party to grow its base, Al Jazeera reports.

international.h: UK arrests 7th suspect in RAF Fairford case
international.b: British police arrested a 22-year-old on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts near RAF Fairford, a base hosting US warplanes.
more: It is the seventh arrest tied to the September 27 incident, which remains largely unexplained.
Police found petrol but no explosives in vans linked to five earlier suspects.

international.h: Kosovo police clash with protesters at parliament
international.b: Police clashed with protesters outside Kosovo's parliament over a bid to curb the Hague war crimes court.
more: Parliament ended its session without passing the changes.

international.h: UN rights council condemns Sudan attacks
international.b: The UN Human Rights Council condemned drone strikes and other attacks on civilians in Sudan and called for a truce.
more: It extended its Sudan fact-finding mission by a vote of 28 to 10, with nine abstentions.
The World Food Programme said an air attack hit a food truck in North Kordofan, killing one person.

international.h: Ethiopia's Abiy vows Red Sea access at swearing-in
international.b: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed began a new five-year term insisting landlocked Ethiopia must have access to the Red Sea.
more: His forces are pushing back Eritrea-backed opposition fighters in Tigray.

international.b: Moroccan journalists described being targeted with Pegasus spyware as Amnesty International makes a new surveillance claim.
more: Journalist Omar Radi says Amnesty's Security Lab found Pegasus on his phone in 2020.
He says he was followed daily while investigating land dispossession; authorities deny the surveillance claims.

international.h: Man deported to Eswatini freed after a year
international.b: A Laotian man the US deported to Eswatini was released from a maximum-security prison after more than a year, his lawyer said.
more: Phone Chomsavanh was one of five immigrants sent to Eswatini in July 2025 under the third-country deportation program.
His lawyer says he is now being deported to Laos.

international.h: Mexico asks US for proof of border shooting
international.b: President Claudia Sheinbaum asked for evidence of shots the US says came from Mexico, which led to a US troop deployment.
more: She said Mexico's forces detected no shots fired from Mexican territory.

international.h: Israeli troops kill one near Hebron
international.b: Troops fired on a car near Bani Naim, killing one Palestinian and seriously injuring two, Palestinian officials said.
more: Israel's military said the car had rammed one of its vehicles.

international.h: Yemen forces reclaim Mocha port from Houthis
international.b: Yemeni government forces say they retook the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha from the Houthis.
more: Turkiye and Pakistan agreed to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca defence pact after Houthi attacks.
Al Jazeera reports Houthi targets were bombed in Yemen and people were injured in attacks on Saudi airports.
Saudi-led forces say they shot down a Houthi missile as fighting rages in Yemen.

international.b: Ethiopian federal forces recaptured Mekelle, the capital of Tigray, amid renewed fighting.
more: Four African leaders issued a joint declaration as the war escalates.

international.h: Nearly 1,500 migrants sent from Malaysia to Myanmar
international.b: Myanmar received nearly 1,500 migrants returned from Malaysia despite UN warnings.

international.h: India protests spread over voter list changes
international.b: Protests have spread across India as opposition groups demand the election chief resign over alleged voter list manipulation.
more: The 'Cockroach' youth movement, which forced the education minister out in July, is helping lead the campaign.
Protesters want Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign and the voter roll revision suspended.
Police detained at least 700 people in Delhi at an earlier protest.

business.h: Paramount, Warner Bros. merge into Skydance
business.b: The $111 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery is set to close Tuesday, creating a company called Skydance.
more: David Ellison becomes CEO, backed by his father Larry Ellison and investors from Saudi Arabia, Qatar and elsewhere.
The deal survived months of protests and legal and regulatory challenges in the US and Europe.

business.h: EPA rollback could hide data center plans
business.b: A proposed EPA rollback could end public notice requirements for many data centers before they are built.
more: The rule targets 'minor sources' of pollution, which many data centers fall under.
Critics say communities could be left in the dark about new air quality risks.

business.h: Faith in college value hits 50-year low
business.b: Just 31% of US adults say a college education is 'very important,' the lowest since Gallup began asking nearly 50 years ago.
more: College costs and student loans are key reasons for the drop.
The souring view comes as many colleges face an enrollment cliff.

business.h: Dollar hits its strongest level in 18 months
business.b: The US dollar is at its strongest since April 2025, driven by high government debt and borrowing for data centers, Marketplace reports.

business.h: Diesel costs drive electric box truck sales
business.b: With diesel averaging $6.32 a gallon, FedEx ordered 2,000 all-electric trucks from Harbinger Motors.
more: California has committed $1 billion to electric truck rebates through 2030.

business.h: US trade deficit jumps 11% to $133 billion
business.b: An early estimate shows the trade deficit rose 11% in August, partly on chip imports for the AI build-out.

business.h: Investors uneasy ahead of Treasury auctions
business.b: The Treasury sells 3-year notes Tuesday, 10-year notes Wednesday and 30-year bonds Thursday after weak demand at recent auctions.

business.h: Americans warming to driverless cars, survey says
business.b: A Cox Automotive survey found about one in five people have ridden in a robotaxi, and 83% of riders said their view improved.
more: Most respondents still want the option of taking the wheel.

business.b: MakerSpace NYC, one of at least 2,000 US community workshops, rents tools to freelancers building their own businesses, Marketplace reports.

science.h: Neutrino hunter Francis Halzen wins Nobel
science.b: Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in physics for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and finding high-energy neutrinos from space.
more: The Nobel committee said his work paved the way for a new kind of astronomy.
Halzen said the news was 'a great surprise.'

science.h: First miniature quasar aimed at Earth spotted
science.b: Astronomers report finding microblazars, small versions of blazars that point at Earth.
more: They may produce some of the mysterious ultra-high-energy cosmic particles that reach Earth.

science.h: Nobel medicine prize goes to optogenetics pioneers
science.b: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine for work on light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.

sports.h: White Sox, Rays both take 2-0 ALDS leads
sports.b: The White Sox beat the Guardians 4-3 and the Rays beat the Yankees 5-2 in Game 2 of the AL Division Series.
more: The White Sox are 4-0 this postseason, all four wins on the road.
The Yankees committed four errors behind Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler.

sports.h: Ovechkin says this season will be his last
sports.b: Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin, the NHL's career goals leader, says his 22nd season will be his final one.
more: He entered the season with 929 goals and turned 41 on September 17.

sports.h: Big Ten admits error by Michigan-WMU refs
sports.b: The Big Ten says the crew from Michigan's disputed win over Western Michigan misapplied a penalty in Nebraska's rout of Maryland.
more: Nebraska's kicker should have been allowed to retry a missed extra point after a roughing the snapper foul.

sports.b: Atlanta beat Los Angeles 3-2 on Sunday to tie their National League Division Series at one game each.
Milwaukee beat San Diego 4-3 on Sunday for a 2-0 lead in their NL Division Series.

local.h: Loophole helps Hochul, Blakeman raise millions
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul and GOP challenger Bruce Blakeman are using a quirk in state law to raise millions of dollars.

local.h: Police name suspects in off-duty cop stabbing
local.b: Commissioner Jessica Tisch identified two men police believe stabbed an off-duty NYPD officer in a Bronx robbery last week.
more: Police named D'Angelo Caraballo, 25, and Sneider Mejia, 24.

local.h: NYC fears migrants will skip health care
local.b: City health officials worry green card rule changes will lead some immigrants to avoid Medicaid and other benefits.
Gov. Hochul declared a disaster emergency as measles spreads across rural upstate New York.

local.h: Bronx woman dies, baby critical after balcony fall
local.b: A Bronx woman died and a baby girl is in critical condition after they fell from a balcony early Tuesday, police said.
more: Someone called 911 from a building at Ollinville and Allerton avenues around 3:38 a.m.

local.h: Relief for NYC tenants losing rent vouchers
local.b: Nearly 6,300 NYC households losing federal rental aid may get to replace their vouchers and stay in their apartments.
more: HUD issued new guidance after letting the earlier aid expire caused fear among tenants and landlords.

local.h: Blind man cut from grand jury can sue NY
local.b: A judge ruled a blind man dismissed from a Brooklyn grand jury can sue New York for discrimination.
more: Albert Elia, 52, says the judge barred him from voting on cases with visual evidence and denied accommodations.

local.h: Gatorade recall reaches New York and New Jersey
local.b: More than 122,000 cases of Gatorade in 37 states are recalled because some bottles may contain unlisted food dyes.

local.h: NYPD detective forced out over false statements
local.b: A Brooklyn detective who admitted giving false information in an investigation was forced to retire after 18 years.

periods.name: This Afternoon
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 65. Northwest wind around 11 mph.

periods.name: Tonight
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 47. Northwest wind around 6 mph becoming calm  after midnight.

periods.name: Wednesday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 68. Light southwest wind becoming south 6 to 11 mph in the morning.

periods.name: Wednesday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 58. Southwest wind 10 to 13 mph.

periods.name: Thursday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 74. West wind 9 to 11 mph.

periods.name: Thursday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 59.

localgood.h: American chestnut returns to the Bronx Zoo
localgood.b: The Bronx Zoo is getting 25 blight-resistant chestnut saplings to help restore a tree nearly wiped out for over a century.

localgood.h: Late-night soccer returns to five NYC parks
localgood.b: One soccer field in each borough will stay lit until 2 a.m. this fall and next spring, after a summer pilot drew 4,500 players.
